summary: Digiday reports Ruggable is shifting budget from Meta ads into ShopMy creators, with its CMO saying it doesn't need bottom-of-funnel affiliate networks while ShopMy converts so well.
Dub added AI screening of partner program applications, letting brands write rules like 'reject partners who plan to promote us via coupon sites'.
Amazon confirmed Q3 earnings on October 29, and one Amazon Influencer says creator rewards haven't updated since the start of the month.
Smaller updates came from YouTube Shopping (an APAC campaign), LTK (15 years) and Lnk.Bio (email signup forms). Nothing new from Lasso, URLgenius or Button.

items.title: Amazon Influencer: creator rewards not updating since the start of the month
items.why: One creator says their monthly rewards progress has shown 'not enough data' all month. It's a single report, but payout visibility is something creators watch closely.

items.title: Amazon will share its Q3 2026 earnings on October 29
Ruggable’s new ad spend strategy shifts focus to ShopMy creators
items.why: Ruggable moved about 10% of its spend from Meta ads into creators and TV, and its CMO said it doesn't need bottom-of-funnel affiliate networks because ShopMy works so well for sales. Brands are starting to treat creator storefront platforms as their main affiliate channel.

items.title: Dub can now auto-screen partner program applications using plain-English rules
items.why: Dub keeps adding affiliate program management features to what started as a link tool.

items.title: YouTube Shopping rolls out 16 films across six markets in APAC campaign
LTK marks 15 years of creator-led shopping
Lnk.Bio adds embedded Sender.net email signup forms to link-in-bio pages
